## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Chán-mìyào fǎ jīng* (T613) is a three-fascicle Mahāyāna meditation manual ascribed in the canonical bibliography to Kumārajīva 鳩摩羅什 ([鳩摩羅什](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%B3%A9%E6%91%A9%E7%BE%85%E4%BB%80)) and his Cháng'ān team. It presents a sequenced program of *kasiṇa* / impurity / loving-kindness / mindfulness-of-the-buddha *dhyāna* leading toward the visualization of the Buddha — overlapping in part with the [KR6i0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0251) *Zuòchán sānmèi jīng* 坐禪三昧經 (T614) and the *Pratyutpanna-samādhi* tradition.

**Abstract**

A central work of early-fifth-century Chinese *chán* practice, datable to Kumārajīva's Cháng'ān period (401–413 CE). Modern scholarship — notably Yamabe Nobuyoshi (1999) — has shown that T613 contains substantial Chinese-composed elements alongside Indic source material; it should be read as a compilation/redaction by Kumārajīva's circle of older Sarvāstivāda *yoga* sources combined with vivid visualization material that may be partly Chinese in origin. Together with [KR6i0251](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0251), [KR6i0252](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0252), [KR6i0253](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0253), [KR6i0254](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0254) it forms the core Kumārajīva-period meditation corpus.
